Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali, Senior Advocate instructed by Syed Mahbubar Rahman, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioners

case_source: (From the judgment and decree dated 25.01.2018 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No.37 of 2017)
full_judgment:
Abu Bakar Siddiquee J. This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated 25.01.2018 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No.37 of 2017 allowing the appeal.

2. The facts, relevant for disposal of this petition, are that the present respondents as plaintiffs instituted. Title Suit No.94 of 2016 in the Court of Joint District Judge, Barguna for setting aside the ex-parte decree dated 25.09.2012 passed by the First Court of Joint District Judge, Barguna in Title Suit No.10 of 2009. In the suit, the plaintiffs, on 10.01.2017, filed an application for staying further proceedings of Execution Case No.04 of 2016 arising out of Title Suit No.10 of 2009. The learned Judge of the trial Court rejected such application for stay and also dis-missed the suit summarily at this initial stage stating that the suit is not maintain-able. Against such order of dismissal, the plaintiff who was defendant in partition suit being No.10 of 2009 moved before the High Court Division and obtained Rule which was made absolute subsequently. The plaintiff in original suit being No.10 of 2009 as petitioner filed the present petition for leave to appeal. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, is that the suit lands originally belonged to Chhaferuddin, Hochanuddin and others. Their names were correctly recorded in CS Khatian mentioning their respective shares. The said recorded tenants and Hochanuddin while enjoying and possessing the suit land, Hochanuddin died leaving behind two wives, namely, Chhahera Bibi and Kadbhanu Bibi. Kadbhanu Bibi gave birth to one son, namely, Amzat Ali and three daughters, namely, Bibishan, Kulsum and Orful. Other wife, Chhahera Bibi gave birth to two sons, namely, Afchher Ali and Hazrat Ali and 4(four) daughters, namely, Gedi Bibi, Duli Bibi, Barojan, Alekjan. One of the wives, namely, Chhahera Bibi got married to a recorded tenant, Chhaferuddin. The daughter of Hochanuddin named Bibishan died leaving behind 4(four) daughters, namely, Hamida, Rokeya, Rahila and Habibunnessa along with mother named Kadbhanu, one brother Amzad Ali and two sisters, namely, Kulsum and Orful. Kulsum died leaving behind her full sister, Orful Bibi and step brother Hazrat Ali and Orful Bibi died leaving behind only son, Abdur Rahim and only daughter, Chherjan Bibi. Amzad Ali died leaving behind his mother, Kadbhanu, two full sisters, namely, Kulsum and Orful Bibi.

3. Afchher Ali, the son of Hochanuddin, died leaving behind his mother, Chhahera Bibi, full brother, Hazrat Ali and 4(four) full sisters, namely, Gedi Bibi, Duli Bibi, Barojan and Alekjan, Dull Bibi died leaving behind her mother, Chhahera Bibi, one daughter, Kadbhanu (according to plaint), two full brothers, namely, Afchher Ali, Hazrat Ali, three full sisters, namely, Gedi Bibi, Barojan and Alekjan as her legal heirs to inherit her properties. Gedi Bibi died leaving behind her mother, Chhahera Bibi, one daughter, Jamina Khatun, two full brothers, namely, Afchher Ali and Hazrat Ali and two sisters, namely, Barojan and Alekjan. Barojan died leaving behind her heirs. Hazrat Ali inherited the share of Jamina Khatun, daughter of Gedi Bibi. Alekjan (wrongly written "Samettban") Bibi, while enjoying and possessing her share, transferred her entire share in favour of Mohammad. Ali and Azahar Ali, they turned it to Hazrat Ali.

4. Said Hazrat Ali died leaving behind his two sons, namely, Chan Miah (plaintiff No.1), Sona Miah (defendant No.9) and two daughters: plaintiff Nos.2 and 3.

5. One of the purchasers named Ismail died leaving behind wife- Mairam Bibi, one son-Tajem Ali and one daughter-Urfur Bibi as his legal heirs and subsequently, Mairam Bibi died leaving behind her son, Tajem Ali and daughter-Urfur Bibi. Tajem Ali died leaving behind his wife-Chan Baru, and only son-Anowar Hossain. Urfur Bibi died leaving behind her husband, Hazrat Ali and only son, Chan Mia. Chan Baru died leaving behind her second husband named Akon Ali, one son, Anowar Hossain and three daughters, namely, Anowara, Pearu and Golbhanu. Johura Bibi died leaving behind her three sons, namely, Meher Ali, Siddique and Sahar Ali and only daughter, Moyful. Said Meher Ali died leaving behind his wife, two full brothers and only full sister. Said brother, Siddique died leaving behind his wife, Surjoban, full brother, Sahar Ali (wrongly written "Goher") and full sister, Moyful and Moyful transferred her entire share in favour of Kashem and others. Said Sahar Ali died leaving behind his wife, Aysnan Bibi and only son Safej, and two daughter, namely, Azitonnessa and Jobetonnessa.

6. The CS recorded tenant, Chhaferuddin died leaving behind his two wives named Aishan @ Ayna Bibi and Chhahera Bibi, two sons named Kashem and Hashem and one daughter, Fulshan. Said Fulshan, daughter of Chhaferuddin, died leaving behind her mother, Ayna Bibi, two full brothers, Hashem Ali and Kashem Ali. Ayna Bibi died leaving behind her two sons, namely, Kashem Ali and Hashem Ali. Said Hashem Ali died leaving behind his wife, Senai Bibi and only son, Sanu Miah. Kashem Ali died leaving behind his only daughter named Golbhanu.

7. The CS recorded tenant, Yasinuddin while enjoying and possessing his share died leaving behind his mother, Chherbhanu, two full brothers, namely, Dalu and Lalu as his legal heirs. Said Chherbhanu died leaving behind her two sons, namely, Dalu and Lalu. Lalu died leaving behind his four sons, namely, Abdul, Ganjar, Chhattar, Rakmon and two daughters, namely, Bibishan and Sufia. Said recorded tenant, Yasinuddin died leaving behind his heirs, Abdul Jabbar and others and they have instituted Title Suit No.187 of 1977 before the then Munsif (now the Assistant Judge), Barguna and the said suit was dismissed on contest and an appeal bearing No.65 of 1987 was being preferred which had been allowed and the defendants preferred Civil Revision No.2759 of 1996 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule which was discharged on 29.10.2007.

8. Defendant Nos.2, 12, 33-38, 40-42, 69 and 72 contested the suit by filing written statement contending, inter alia, that this suit cannot run in the present form and is barred by limitation and defect of parties. It is also barred by res-judicata. The plaintiff falsely and fraudulently filed the instant snit. 5.76 acres land is in possession of defendant Nos.2/14-35 and others, Defendant No. 37 claimed that he is in possession of .74 acre land. Defendant No.72 contended that he is in possession of .60 acre land and defendant Nos.12, 33/69-71/78 claimed saham of (.60+2.16) =2.66 acres land. Defendant Nos.36/38/40-42 contended that they are in possession of 2.88 acres land. Therefore, the suit is liable to be dismissed with costs.

9. The partition suit being No.10 of 2009 was decreed ex-parte on 25.09.2012 passed by the trial Court. The present respondents as plaintiff filed the present regular suit for setting aside the ex-parte decree dated 25.09.2012 on the ground of non service of summons in which the present respondent filed an application for staying further proceeding of Title Execution Case No.04 of 2016 arising out Title Suit No.10 of 2009. The learned Judge of the trial Court has rejected not only the application for stay but also dis-missed the suit as being non-maintainable.

10. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the plaintiffs preferred First Appeal No.37 of 2017 before the High Court Division, the High Court Division after hearing the appeal allowed the same setting aside the judgment and decree dated 10.01.2017 and thereby restored the original suit being No.94 of 2016.

11. Against the judgment and order of the High Court Division, the defendants filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1028 of 2018 before this Division seeking leave.

12. Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali, learned Counsel, appearing on behalf of the petitioners, submits present respondents as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.94 of 2016 for setting aside an ex-parte decree on the ground that summonses were not duly served upon them in the original suit and the plaintiffs (present respondents) filed an application for staying the execution proceeding Title Execution being No.04 of 2015 arising out from Titles Suit No. 10 of 2009 and only point for determination for the trial Court to ascertain as to whether the said application for staying would be sustainable. He further submits that the present petitioners as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.10 of 2009 in the Court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Barguna for partition of the suit lands impleading present respondents and others as defendants. Wherein several sets of the defendants contested the said partition suit including the full brother of present respondent named Sona Miah after receiving the summonses of the Court, but the present respondents (plaintiffs in Title Suit No.94 of 2016) did not contest the said suit though the summonses were duly served upon them and it is evident from the decree of Title Suit No.10 of 2009 that the addresses of all defendants are the same and they are residing in the same mess and the preliminary decree of the said suit made final, but respondent Nos.1-3 instituted subsequent Title Suit No.94 of 2016 long delay and on the mere plea that the summonses were not duly served upon them by suppressing the material facts and as such, the trial Court rightly dismissed the suit, but the High Court Division passed an order of restoration of original suit after setting aside the order of trial Court. The learned Counsel further submits that admittedly the judgment and decree dated 25.09.2012 has been challenged by one defendant named Abdur Rahman in Title Appeal No.69 of 2012 impleading the present defendants as respondent Nos.9-20 in the said title appeal by mentioning their addresses and their summonses have been duly served in the said title appeal, but they are reluctant to proceed with the said appeal and at a stage, the said appeal is dismissed affirming those of the trial Court and accordingly, the preliminary judgment and decree of the trial Court is made final and the defendants of the original partition suit tried to create an obstacle to enjoy the fruit of the said judgment and decree passed in favour of the plaintiffs by filing the vexatious suit and the trial Court rightly dismissed the same, but the High Court Division as the appellate Court without going through materials on record very illegally restored the original suit being No.10 of 2009 after setting aside the well-founded judgment and decree. He finally submits that Title Suit No.94 of 2016 is not maintainable without challenging the final decree passed in Decree Execution Case No.04 of 2016 arising out of judgment and decree dated 25.09.2012 passed in Title Suit No.10 of 2009; the High Court Division ought to have considered the said moot question in deciding First Appeal No.37 of 2017, but most illegally set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court by the judgment and decree dated 25.01.2018.

13. Mr. Parietal Chandra Guha, learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the respondents, in his submissions, supported the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division.

14. We have heard the learned Advocates of both the parties and perused the materials on record.

15. Title Suit No.10 of 2009 was a partition suit instituted by the present petitioners as plaintiffs against the present respondents, Chan Miah and others and that summonses and notices were alleged to have been duly served upon all the defendants of that suit and thereafter, the suit has been decreed against defendant Nos.12/33/61-- -71/78/72/36/38/80-42/37 on contest and ex-parte against the rests. The defendant (in Title Suit No.94 of 2016) i.e. present petitioners have come with an allegation that the allegation regarding non-service of summons does not hold any water whereas present respondents, Chart Mia and others filed Title Suit No.94 of 2016 claiming that due to non-service of summons decree passed in Title Suit No.10 of 2009 is illegal, inoperative and liable to be set aside.

16. Mr. A.J. Mohammad Ali, learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the present petitioners argued that although on the ground of non-service of summons, defendant Nos.1 to 3 of Title Suit No.10 of 2009 instituted Title Suit No.94 of 2016 against the present petitioners, but they were duly served with summonses and notices. He further adds that the brother of plaintiff No.1, Chan Mia appeared and contested Title Suit No.10 of 2009 whereas the three plaintiff-respondent demanded that they were not ever served with summonses and notices. He further adds that Title Suit No.94 of 2016 was filed beyond the statutory period of limitation and as such, that suit is hopelessly barred by limitation. He also argued that Title Suit No.94 of 2016 is not maintainable without challenging the final decree passed in Decree Execution Case No.04 of 2016 arising out of judgment and decree dated 25.09.2012 passed in Title Suit No.10 of 2009 and as an appellate Court, the High Court Division ought to have considered the said moot question in deciding First Appeal No.37 of 2017, but most illegally setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court by the judgment and decree dated 25.01.2018 and as such, the judgment and order of the High Court Division is liable to be set aside.

17. According to the procedure, an ex-parte decree can be impeached in three distinct ways:-

l. By filing a miscellaneous case under Order IX Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

2. By filing an appeal before the appellate Court.

3. By filing a regular suit in the trial Court.

18. There plaintiff-respondents have chosen the third category intending to assail the impugned ex-parte decree, that is, the plaintiff-respondent filed a regular suit on the ground of non-service summons and notices upon them. The learned trial Court has opined in the initial stage that the present suit is not maintainable. It has been further opined that the plaintiff-respondent earlier preferred an appeal bearing No.69 of 2012 which has been dismissed subsequently and that whenever an execution proceeding has been started, the plaintiff-respondents have initiated this malafide suit for setting aside the ex-parte decree on the flimsy ground of non-service of summons. It has been revealed that the ground of dismissal should be determined after taking or recording evidence. The learned Judge of the Division Bench of the High Court Division held the view that in any way, the suit cannot be dismissed on such ground of maintainability at initial stage. It has been further held that the learned Judge of the Court below dismissed the suit at his own initiative, but the reason assigned will not come within the ambit of Order-VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure (briefly as the Code). So the impugned judgment and order is illegal and caused a serious miscarriage of justice.

19. For the convenience of understanding the provisions of Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure can be reviewed which reads as under:

"Rule ll-The plaint shall be rejected on the following issues:

(a) Where it does not disclose a cause of action.

(b) Where the relief claimed is under-valued, and the plaintiff, on being required by the Court to correct the valuation within a time to be fixed by the court fails to do so;

(c) Where the relief claimed is properly valued, but the plaint is written upon paper insufficiently stamped and the plaintiff, on being required by the Court to supply the requisite stamp-paper within a time to be fixed by the Court, fails to do so.

(d) Where the suit appears from the statement in the plaint to be barred by any law"

20. On perusal of the materials on record, it transpires that the plaintiffs (defendant in Title Suit No.10 of 2009) instituted Title Suit No.94 of 2016 for setting aside the ex-parte decree on the ground that summonses were not served upon them in that suit. The only point assigned in the impugned judgment and order is whether the execution case of the former suit should be stayed or not? But the learned Judge of the trial Court in course of deciding the fate of stay petition has dismissed the suit summarily. The learned Judge of the trial Court finds in the following verbatim:-

“বিজ্ঞ কৌশুলীর বক্তব্য শুনিলাম। নথি সমূহ পর্যালোচনায় দেখা যায় মূল দেং ১০/২০০৯ তে এই বাদীপক্ষ বিবাদী শ্রেণীভুক্ত ছিল। তারা ছিল ১/৩/৪নং মূল বিবাদী মূল নথি দৃষ্টে দেখা যায়। ১৬/০৭/২০০৯ইং তারিখে তাদের উপর যথারীতি সমন/নোটিশ জারী হলে তারা প্রতিদ্বন্বিতা করে। নথি দৃষ্টে আরো দেখা যায় যে, নোটিশ জারী হওয়ায় ত বৎসর পরে বাদী প্রতিদ্বন্দিতা বিবাদীপক্ষ প্রতিদন্বিতা করিয়াছে। ফলে দোতরফা সূত্রে ডিক্রী হয় বিগত ইং ২৫/০৯২০১২ তারিখে নিষ্পত্তি আপীল ৬৯/২০১২ দায়ের হইলে ২৩/১০/২০১৪ তারিখে মুল দেং ১০/২০০৯ মোকদ্দমার রায় ডিক্রী জারী মোকদ্দরার কার্যক্রম সম্পন্ন হয় এবং উহা পূর্ন সন্তষ্টিতে নিষ্পত্তি হয়। এমতাবস্থায় অদ্যকার দাখিলী দরখাস্তখানা সরাসরি নামঞ্জুর করা হইল। উপরোক্ত পর্যালোচনার আলোকে মোকদ্দমাটি গ্রহনযোগ্যতা নাই মর্মে প্রতীয়মান হওয়ায় তা খারিজ যোগ্য। কোর্ট ফি সঠিক । অতএব, আদেশ হয় যে, অন্র দেওয়ানী মোকদমাটি গ্রহণযোগ্যতা শুনানী অন্তে সরাসরি খারিজ করা হইল ।”

21. Now the question that falls for determination as to how far the trial Court is justified in dismissing the suit summarily in course of deciding an application for staying the further proceeding of Title Execution No.04 of 2015.

22. In this respect, the learned Judge of the High Court Division has observed in the following verbatim:-

"Now coming to clause (d) of rule 11 of the order 7 it appears that clause (d) of the rule authorizes the rejection of a plaint when the suit appears from the statements in the plaint to be barred by any law. This clause applies when it appear from the statements in the plaint that the suit is barred but it has no application where there is no clear or specific admission in the plaint suggesting that the suit is barred. This clause is attracted only when on the admitted facts as appearing from the plaint itself the suit is prima facie barred. As for instance when from the statements made in the plaint it appears that the cause of action arose beyond the period of limitation fixed under the statute and no indication is given that limitation has been saved, the plaint may be rejected. In a proper case, when it appears to be barred by limitation, the plaint may be allowed to be amended without rejection. It is not mandatory for the Court to reject the pliant. It may ask the plaintiff to amend it so as to make suit maintainable. Where the plaintiff failed to comply with such an order, the Court may reject the plaint. Reference may be made to the cases reported in 18 CWN 1340 AIR 1928 Oudh 495 and AIR 1953 Ca1.222. "

23. The learned Judge of the Division Bench of the High Court Division further observed that the learned trial Court below without considering the materials on record as well as prevailing law of the land dismissed the suit and thereby committed an error of law and as such, the order of the trial Court is liable to be interfered with. The Division Bench of the High Court Division further held that the dismissal order in its entirety is not well founded in the facts and circumstances of the case and as such, the preponderant judicial views emerging out of the authorities led us to hold that the judgment and decree of the trial Court suffers from legal infirmities which calls for interference by this Court.

24. We have gone through the finding and decisions of the learned Judge of the Division Bench of the High Court Division. Since the dismissal order passed by the trial Court does not come under the mischief under Order VII, rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, we have no option but to agree with the finding and decision of the learned Judge of the High Court Division. We also hold the view that the learned Judges of the High Court Division have made threadbare discussion about the facts and circumstances of the case and so also relevant law and left no stone unturned in deciding the appeal and there is no legal infirmity or misreading or non-consideration of evidence on record.

25. The question of limitation is also a mixed question of fact and law and as such, it is not wise to dispose of this issue on the score of rejection of plaint at an initial stage of the suit.

26. Having considered those facts and circumstances, materials on record, we find no illegality and infirmity in the impugned judgment.

27. Therefore, we find no reason to interfere with the decision and findings of the High Court Division.

28. Accordingly, this civil petition is dis-missed without any order as to costs.

End.
